criterion: The run board separates runs into columns by status, so a run paused for a person sits in its own column rather than behind a filter.
evaluation_rule: The run board is the signed-in page listing a project's runs. Yes if runs are arranged into visible columns headed by their status, with a column for runs that are waiting on a person. No if the runs appear as one flat list that has to be filtered or sorted to find the waiting ones.

criterion: The workflow canvas shows the steps as boxes on a dotted ground joined by curved edges, with the step list beside the drawing.
evaluation_rule: The canvas is the page for one workflow inside a project. Yes if the steps are drawn as connected boxes over a dotted background with a list of the same steps alongside. No if the workflow appears only as a list or a table with no drawn graph.

criterion: A new step joins a workflow as a fresh row at the end of the step list rather than through a pop-up.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the control for adding a step puts an editable row at the bottom of the step list in place. No if adding a step opens a modal dialog or moves the reader to a separate page.

criterion: An approval decision opens its own confirmation page carrying the run identifier and the decision.
evaluation_rule: Yes if pressing approve or reject moves the reader to a page whose whole content is the confirmation, naming which run was decided and which way. No if the only feedback is a small transient message over the previous page.

criterion: Console navigation drills down through project, then workflows or runs, then one item, with a breadcrumb back up.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the signed-in pages show a trail of the levels above the current one and each level is reachable from that trail. No if the console is a flat sidebar with no sense of depth, or the trail is absent on the detail pages.

criterion: Body text across the public site is a warm off-white against the near-black ground rather than pure white.
evaluation_rule: Yes if paragraph text reads as a soft light grey with a warm cast, sitting still against the dark background. No if paragraph text is a bright pure white that shimmers against the ground.

criterion: The warm orange-to-red gradient appears on one action per page and nothing else wears that fill.
evaluation_rule: The call-to-action gradient is the hot orange-into-red fill. Yes if at most one control per page carries it and every other control is a different treatment. No if several controls on one page share that fill, or a non-interactive surface carries it.

criterion: Each card carries a single hairline of warm light along its top edge, so the card looks lit from above rather than outlined.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the panels on the marketing routes show a faint warm line along their upper edge alone. No if the panels are drawn with an even border on all four sides, or with no edge treatment at all.

criterion: The path from a queued run through its detail to the approvals queue reads as one journey that always offers a next step.
evaluation_rule: Yes if a reader can move from the board to one run, from that run to the decision, and back to the board without typing an address or using the browser back button. No if any of those steps leaves the reader with no way onward.

criterion: An empty list in the console tells a reader what would appear there.
evaluation_rule: Yes if an empty workflow list, run board, approvals queue or catalogue result set renders a sentence saying what would appear there. No if an empty list renders as blank space or an error.

criterion: Content on the marketing routes arrives once on entering the window and stays arrived when the reader scrolls back up.
evaluation_rule: Yes if blocks fade and rise slightly as they enter the window, and do not fade back out or replay when the reader scrolls up past them again. No if the reveal reverses on scroll up, or if nothing moves at all.

criterion: The keyboard reaches every control on the pricing route, the integrations catalogue and the run board, with an outline marking the focused control.
evaluation_rule: Yes if tabbing moves through the navigation, the forms and the console controls in a sensible order with a visible outline on the focused one. No if the outline is absent, or if it is only a change of brightness that cannot be told from the pointer state.

criterion: At a phone width the layout becomes a single stack with nothing running off the side of the screen.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the pricing table, the catalogue and the run board each stack into one column at a narrow width with no sideways scrolling of the page. No if content overflows horizontally or a navigation target becomes unreachable.

criterion: A panel on the marketing site lifts or grows when the pointer rests over that panel.
evaluation_rule: Yes if pointing at a card makes it lift, grow or bounce. No if pointing at a card changes only its colour and light while the card stays exactly where it is.

criterion: The enterprise route offers a free-trial action beside its sales action.
evaluation_rule: Yes if the enterprise route shows any control offering a free trial or a self-serve signup. No if its only action is the one asking the reader to contact sales.
